transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: I hear you—after three months with nothing to show for it, you’d be skeptical. Before I explain the difference, what were you hoping that agency would actually deliver for you (more inbound calls, booked jobs, better follow-up, something else)?
User: I wanted more booked appointments and reliable follow-up, but they vanished after I signed the contract.
Agent: Got it—so you signed, and then they basically disappeared, and you never got the booked appointments or follow-up you were expecting. When a new call comes in and you’re tied up, what usually happens—does it go to voicemail or does someone pick it up?
User: It usually goes to voicemail, and we end up missing about 18 calls a week.
Agent: Mhm—18 a week is a lot, and voicemail usually means they just move on. What kind of business is this for—what do you do?
User: It's for my dental practice, Cole Family Dental. We're losing potential patients, and it's frustrating.
Agent: Got it—Cole Family Dental, and those missed voicemails are costing you potential patients, which is beyond frustrating. When those 18 calls get missed, do you have anyone consistently calling them back the same day, or do a lot of them slip to the next day?
User: We try to call back, but it's often the next day. Many times, they've moved on by then.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—next day is usually too late, especially for a dental office. Has anyone ever showed you the math on what those 18 missed calls a week might be costing you?
User: No, they haven't. But considering 60% would book and spend $240 each, I assume it's substantial.
Agent: Yeah—that’s substantial: with 18 missed calls/week, 60% booking, and $240 per patient, you’re looking at roughly **$11,200/month** slipping away when those calls hit voicemail and get returned the next day.  

Cool—it's a 20-minute walkthrough with Jay where we’ll show exactly how we recover those missed calls and what the numbers look like for Cole Family Dental… what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Promises are free. What happens after the demo? Will my calls still get missed once I sign?
Agent: Totally fair—after the demo, if you decide to move forward, we set it up so missed calls don’t just go to voicemail; they get answered and turned into booked appointments (and if your team is free, it hands off to them).  

Would you be open to a 20-minute walkthrough this week so Jay can show you exactly what happens after you sign?
User: Okay... one demo. But I'm watching closely. Let's schedule this week.
Agent: Fair—and I wouldn’t expect anything less. What’s your first name?
User: I'm Bianca. Just want to make sure this demo is worth my time after past experiences.
Agent: Got it, Bianca—and yeah, protecting your time makes total sense. What’s your last name?
User: Cole. Just need to see how this truly works before any commitment.
Agent: Makes sense, Bianca Cole—seeing it work is the only thing that matters. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: Yes, that's fine. But remember, I'm in Mountain/Phoenix time, so schedule accordingly.
Agent: Got it—Mountain/Phoenix time. Would you prefer later today or tomorrow for the demo?
User: Tomorrow works. Please ensure it's Mountain/Phoenix time. Look forward to seeing how this can help.
Agent: Perfect—tomorrow I can get you in as soon as **12:45 PM** or **4:30 PM** Mountain/Phoenix time. Which works?
User: Let's go with 12:45 PM Mountain/Phoenix time. I'll be ready to see how this works.
Agent: So that’s **tomorrow, Aug 28 at 12:45 PM** Mountain/Phoenix time, correct?
User: Yes, that's correct. Tomorrow, August 28 at 12:45 PM Mountain/Phoenix time. Looking forward to it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Hmm—looks like the calendar is showing a conflict at **12:45 PM** tomorrow (Mountain/Phoenix time), so it won’t let me lock that in.  

Would **4:30 PM** tomorrow work instead?
User: Sure, but remember I'm in Mountain/Phoenix time. It's important the timing aligns correctly.
Agent: Got it—Mountain/Phoenix time only. Would **4:30 PM tomorrow (Mountain/Phoenix time)** work for you?
User: 4:30 PM Mountain/Phoenix time works for me. I'll be ready to see how this demo can help.
Agent: One moment while I get 4:30 PM locked in for you.
Agent: Thanks, Bianca! You’re booked for **tomorrow, Aug 28 at 4:30 PM Mountain/Phoenix time**, and you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—so you can add it to your calendar in one click or reschedule if you need to.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Great, I'll wait for the confirmation. Remember, it's Mountain/Phoenix time. Looking forward to the demo.
Agent: Perfect—it's set for tomorrow at 4:30 PM Mountain/Phoenix time. Really glad you called, Bianca. Jay’s looking forward to it—have a great day. Bye!
